title: The Golden Horseshoe Racecourse
teaser: The favourite came in last, though the stable owner had bet everything on him. Ernest Weiss was found in the stalls before the final bell. Someone knew all too well that the favourite wouldn't win, and someone helped make sure he didn't.

habits.label: Spurs
clues: The favourite's stall door has fresh scratches at heel height, the kind spurs leave. The culprit wears boots with spurs.
A rowel broken off a spur lies in the straw by Weiss's body. The culprit wears boots with spurs.

habits.label: Horseshoe charm
habits.habit: A little brass horseshoe charm in the pocket
clues: A little brass horseshoe, rubbed shiny by fingers, glints in the straw of the stall. The culprit carries a horseshoe charm.
Weiss's fist is clenched around someone else's brass horseshoe, and Weiss himself never believed in luck. The culprit carries a horseshoe charm.

habits.label: Hoof scar
habits.habit: A scar from a hoof on the forehead
clues: At 15:15 someone in the grandstand saw a person with a horseshoe-shaped scar on the forehead at the stable gate. The culprit has a hoof scar on their forehead.
Weiss's notebook says: "The one Zvezda kicked in forty-eight is hanging around the stalls again." The culprit has a hoof scar on their forehead.

habits.label: Stutters
clues: From the feed store someone heard an argument by the stalls, and one voice stuttered badly on every word. The culprit stutters.
At 15:05 someone rang the weighing room and, stumbling over every syllable, asked them to hold back the favourite. The culprit stutters.

habits.label: Works out odds
habits.habit: Works out bets and odds in their head
clues: On the back of a race card by the body, the favourite's odds have been recalculated in pencil without a single mistake. The culprit works out odds in their head.
The odds for each race, adjusted for the jockeys' weights, are chalked on the weighing-room wall. The culprit can work out bets in their head in an instant.

habits.label: Sour apples
clues: There's an Antonovka apple core with human tooth marks in the stall's manger. The culprit loves sour apples.
There's a scattering of apple pips and an Antonovka stalk by the stable gate. The culprit munches sour apples.

habits.label: Gap-toothed
clues: At 15:10 the weighing room heard a lisping voice speak to Weiss, as if air were whistling through a gap in the teeth. The culprit is missing a front tooth.
A sugar lump in the stall has a bite mark with an empty space in the middle. The culprit is missing a front tooth.

habits.label: Checked scarf
clues: A scrap of green checked silk hangs on a nail in the stall. The culprit wears a green-checked scarf.
People in the owners' box remember someone in a green checked scarf hurrying to the stables before the last race. The culprit wears a green-checked scarf.

habits.label: Red clay
habits.habit: Shoes caked in the paddock's red clay
clues: A trail of red clay runs from the paddock to the stalls, and there's no other soil like it at the racecourse. The culprit's shoes are caked in paddock clay.
There are lumps of red clay with a heel print on the edge of the manger. The culprit's shoes are covered in paddock clay.

habits.label: Stopwatch
clues: A stopwatch stopped at one minute forty, the favourite's warm-up time, lies in the straw by the body. The culprit carries a stopwatch on a cord.
Weiss's fingers are clutching a torn cord with the little clip from a stopwatch. The culprit carries a stopwatch on a cord.

habits.label: Horse cufflinks
habits.habit: Cufflinks shaped like a horse's head
clues: A silver cufflink shaped like a horse's head was found under the stall partition. The culprit wears horse's-head cufflinks.
Someone else's horse's-head cufflink is caught on the cuff of Weiss's jacket. The culprit wears horse's-head cufflinks.

habits.label: Knows bloodlines
clues: The name of the favourite's dam on the stall plate has been corrected in chalk, and corrected right. The culprit knows horses' bloodlines by heart.
There's a note in someone else's hand in Weiss's pocket: "Grandson of Zenith, no good on heavy ground." The culprit knows horses' bloodlines.

habits.label: Hoof oil
clues: The stall bolt is shiny with fresh hoof oil, though the favourite wasn't groomed today. The culprit smells of hoof oil.
Weiss's jacket has a greasy handprint that smells of hoof oil. The culprit's hands smell of hoof oil.

habits.label: Pitchfork calluses
habits.habit: Hard pitchfork calluses on the palms
clues: Weiss's wrists are grazed, as if he'd been held by hands as rough as a grater. The culprit has pitchfork calluses on their palms.
A pitchfork has been dropped by the stall, and there are flakes of rough, peeled skin on its handle. The culprit has pitchfork calluses.

habits.label: Flat cap
habits.habit: An eight-panel flat cap pulled over the eyes
clues: The cloth-covered button from the top of an eight-panel cap was found in the straw. The culprit wears an eight-panel cap.
Someone in the grandstand saw a person at the stable gate in an eight-panel cap pulled down over their eyes. The culprit wears a flat cap.

habits.label: Smells of mothballs
clues: The stall by the body reeks of mothballs, strong enough to cover even the smell of horse. The culprit smells of mothballs.
There's a stray wool hair on Weiss's lapel that reeks of mothballs. The culprit's clothes smell of mothballs.

strong: The heavy stall door was torn off its lower hinge so the body could be dragged in. The culprit is physically strong.
An eighty-kilo sack of oats was moved to hide the body. The culprit is physically strong.
quiet: The horses in the neighbouring stalls didn't stir, though they shy at any stranger's footstep. The culprit moves silently.
The stable floorboards creak, but nobody at the entrance heard a thing. The culprit moves silently.
tools: The favourite's shoe was bent with hoof pincers just enough to throw him off his stride. The culprit is handy with tools.
The stall bolt was removed and put back, and there are fresh screwdriver marks on the screws. The culprit is handy with tools.
medic: The bucket by the favourite's stall has a sedative residue, the dose calculated exactly for a horse. The culprit knows about poisons.
A veterinary syringe lies in the stall, and there's a needle mark on Weiss's neck. The culprit knows about poisons.
cash: Bets on the losers are missing from the tote, and the ledger has been doctored. The culprit had access to money.
Half an hour before the race the tote took a big bet against the favourite, with money taken from the stable office. The culprit had access to money.
safe: The safe in the owners' box was opened without force, and Weiss's promissory notes aren't in it. The culprit knows the safe combination.
The accounts office changes its safe combination every week, yet the door has been opened neatly. The culprit knows the safe combination.
keys: The stables are locked before the races, and the lock was opened with its own key. The culprit had keys.
The favourite's stall was unlocked with a key from the shared ring, and the ring is hanging in its place. The culprit had keys.
sched: It all happened while the stable hands stood by the paddock before the last race. The culprit knows the schedule.
Security walks round the stables every forty minutes, and the timing fell exactly between rounds. The culprit knows the schedule.
glasses: A horn arm from a pair of glasses lies in the straw by the body. The culprit wears glasses.
There's the imprint of a frame on the dusty glass of the weighing room, as if someone in glasses pressed their face to it. The culprit wears glasses.
french: The back of a tote ticket has a note in French: "Il ne gagnera pas". The culprit knows French.
There's a letter in French about selling the favourite in Weiss's pocket. The culprit knows French.
smoker: Three Kazbek cigarette ends lie in the stables, where smoking is forbidden. The culprit smokes.
There's fresh ash and a burnt match by the stable gate. The culprit smokes.
driver: Fresh lorry tracks lead from the feed store to the stables, and according to the log the feed lorry never left the garage. The culprit can drive.
The horsebox has been backed up to the stable gate, and the engine is still warm. The culprit can drive.
whistle: Whistling was heard from the stables at about 15:15. The culprit whistles.
People in the paddock remember a tune someone was whistling by the stalls before the race. The culprit whistles.
perfume: The stall by the body smells of heavy perfume, stronger than the smell of hay. The culprit wears heavy perfume.
The race card in Weiss's hand has a spot of thick, sweet perfume on it. The culprit wears heavy perfume.
cane: There are round holes from a walking stick in the soft ground by the stables. The culprit walks with a cane.
At about 15:10 security heard a cane tapping on the stable boards. The culprit walks with a cane.
